title: Nothing is literally doubling down on its smartphone ambitions, contrary to previous report
title_bn: Nothing is literally doubling down on its smartphone ambitions, contrary to previous report
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Nothing suggests it will launch up to six phones in 2027, doubling the total number of phones it released this year.
paragraph1: Andy Walker / Android AuthorityTL;DR Nothing co-founder Akis Evangelidis has revealed that the company may launch twice as many phones in 2027 as it did this year. The executive also reiterated that the US market is a “major priority” for Nothing in the audio segment. Nothing seems to have more products planned for launch this quarter, though Evangelidis didn’t specify if they were phones or other devices. Nothing has largely succeeded in capturing the tech industry’s imagination despite being a relatively new entrant. Following the Phone 1, the company has released multiple flagships, including the Phone 4a Pro earlier this year.
paragraph2: We’re now getting an early glimpse of the company’s ambitious plans for 2027, even as the tech world struggles with the RAM crisis.In an interview with Times Now Tech, Nothing co-founder Akis Evangelidis revealed the company plans to launch twice as many phones in 2027 as it did this year. If our math is accurate, this could potentially mean the release of up to six Nothing devices next year. For reference, Nothing has released three smartphones in 2026, including the vanilla Phone 4a, the Phone 4a Pro, and the Phone 4b. “We’ll share more details closer to launch, but the idea is to have a wider range of smartphones,” Evangelidis said.
paragraph3: The Nothing exec was less optimistic about the future of CMF phones, saying the company is keeping an eye on the market. This comes on the heels of the manufacturer shelving the CMF Phone 3 Pro due to a historic uptick in memory prices.“Even this year, we pulled off the plug quite late. We’re looking at different ways on how we could make it happen for next year. But that’s still in consideration.
paragraph4: We’re staying close to how the memory price will evolve,” he told the publication. At the same time, he added that the “plans are pretty much set” to double the number of Nothing devices in 2027, indicating a big shift in the company’s smartphone strategy.It’s worth pointing out that the co-founder’s words contradict last week’s report that the company would pivot to an AI-first strategy with the launch of a new smartwatch, earbuds, headphones, and speakers. However, Nothing hasn’t commented on this report yet, with Evangelidis only saying in the interview that the company now has “dedicated business units for audio and AI-native products.”We’re also getting confirmation that the manufacturer has more devices in the pipeline for Q3.
paragraph5: However, the exec didn’t specify whether they are phones, smartwatches, audio products, or some of those AI-first products mentioned in the recent report. While reiterating the company’s focus on markets like India, Evangelidis said the US also remains a “major priority,” especially in the headphones and earbuds segment.FollowThank you for being part of our community. title: Kentucky family snubs $26 million offer to convert their farmland into an AI data center — 'they call us old stupid farmers, you know, but we’re not,' says landowner
title_bn: Kentucky family snubs $26 million offer to convert their farmland into an AI data center — 'they call us old stupid farmers, you know, but we’re not,' says landowner
author: TechPulse
excerpt: A Northern Kentucky family has refused an anonymous AI company's $26 million offer to buy their land and transform it into a data center.
paragraph1: (Image credit: Getty Images) According to a WKRC report, an anonymous AI company approached a landowner in Northern Kentucky with an extraordinary $26 million offer to buy a portion of their farmland to build a data center. Despite the life-changing sum, Ida Huddleston and her family, who have owned and cultivated the land for generations, firmly rejected the offer.Go deeper with TH Premium: AI and data centers“They call us old stupid farmers, you know, but we’re not,” Huddleston asserted. “We know whenever our food is disappearing, our lands are disappearing, and we don’t have any water—and that poison. Well, we know we’ve had it.”Delsia Bare, Huddleston’s daughter, shared a short but rich history of their family's land.
paragraph2: For generations, the Huddleston family has been cultivating the soil and providing food for countless families beyond their own. Bare described how their ancestors persevered through some of the nation’s darkest times, such as raising wheat during the Great Depression and helping keep bread lines supplied when much of America was struggling with poverty and hunger.“Stay and hold and feed a nation,” Bare told WKRC. “$26 million doesn’t mean anything.”The AI company, presumed to be one of the major players in the industry, reached out to Huddleston because of the size and the location of the 1,200-acre property. The AI company sought to acquire roughly half of the land for a big data center project.
paragraph3: Farmland in Mason County typically sells for around $6,000 per acre. In an attempt to woo the Huddlestons to sign, the AI company offered $26 million, nearly 10X the local land value. Despite the lucrative offer, Huddleston and her family declined without hesitation.With the AI boom advancing at a breakneck speed, AI companies are competing to construct data centers nationwide. According to Statista, the United States leads the world with more than 4,400 data centers. For comparison, the United Kingdom, which ranks second, has roughly one-eighth that number.
paragraph4: The proliferation of data centers over the last few years has brought many shortcomings. Some include the requirement for enormous amounts of electricity and water to operate; these facilities are stretching the local electrical grids to their limits, with energy bills soaring and depleting the water supply. It is understandable why residents in many areas are refusing to welcome more data centers that jeopardize their quality of life.Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Unfortunately, not everyone has the conviction or financial stability to say no to $26 million. The AI company reportedly contacted several other landowners in the surrounding area.
paragraph5: According to Bare, some landowners caved in and agreed to sell. Despite the Huddleston family's stance and determination to protect their legacy, it appears the AI company will still get to build its data center somewhere nearby. title: Swiggy Bets On Toing, Instamart To Achieve ₹10,000 Cr Adjusted EBITDA By FY31
title_bn: Swiggy Bets On Toing, Instamart To Achieve ₹10,000 Cr Adjusted EBITDA By FY31
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Swiggy is banking on its affordable meals platform Toing and quick commerce business Instamart to achieve a consolidated adjusted EBITDA…
paragraph1: SUMMARYSwiggy is targeting to achieve a consolidated adjusted EBITDA of ₹10,000 Cr by FY31 on the back of Toing and quick commerce segment For its food delivery business, Swiggy expects adjusted EBITDA to increase fivefold from about ₹1,000 Cr in FY26 to ₹5,000 Cr by FY31. To achieve this, the comoany aims to expand affordability initiatives such as Toing On the Swiggy Instamart's front, the company expects the business to continue scaling rapidly over the next five years while benefiting from higher operating leverage Swiggy is banking on its affordable meals platform Toing and quick commerce business Instamart to achieve a consolidated adjusted EBITDA of ₹10,000 Cr by FY31. At its Capital Markets Day, the foodtech major outlined its long-term growth roadmap, projecting an overall gross order value (GOV) of ₹2.5 Lakh Cr by FY31, driven by sustained growth across food delivery, quick commerce, and dining-out. For its food delivery business, Swiggy expects adjusted EBITDA to increase fivefold from about ₹1,000 Cr in FY26 to ₹5,000 Cr by FY31. To achieve this, the company plans to strengthen its core food delivery operations, expand affordability initiatives such as Toing, and drive monetisation through scale efficiencies. Meanwhile, Swiggy is targeting a GOV of ₹1.
paragraph2: 5 Lakh Cr for Instamart by FY31, implying a CAGR of 42% from ₹28,000 Cr in FY26. The company also expects Dineout to generate ₹1,000 Cr in adjusted EBITDA by FY31. Swiggy launched Toing in September last year to offer affordable meal options. Initially launched in Pune, the platform is now available across 50 cities, including Mumbai, Bengaluru, Delhi NCR, Ahmedabad, Kolkata, Chennai, Jaipur, Chandigarh and Patna. In Q1 FY27, Toing and Crew together generated revenue of ₹51 Cr, while losses widened to ₹131 Cr as the company continued investing in the two offerings. Swiggy said it is expanding its affordability initiatives to attract consumers who have so far stayed away from online food delivery because of pricing. It added that two out of every three users acquired through Toing are either new to the platform or inactive users returning to it.
paragraph3: Instamart, meanwhile, achieved contribution margin breakeven in Q1 FY27, with contribution margin turning positive at 0.2% on a GOV of ₹7,907 Cr. Following the Capital Markets Day presentation, Swiggy shares rose as much as 5.6% to an intraday high of ₹305.10 on the BSE today. The stock later pared some gains and was trading marginally lower at ₹288.7 apiece at 14:53 IST, taking the company’s market capitalisation to ₹79,621.
paragraph4: 24 Cr Inside Swiggy’s Affordability Playbook Swiggy said affordability remains one of the biggest hurdles to increasing ordering frequency, with nearly 70% of users placing food delivery orders less than once a month. To address this, Toing offers lower-priced meals without packaging or platform fees. According to the company, the platform is designed to encourage users to order more frequently and expand the overall online food delivery market instead of merely competing for market share. Swiggy said Toing is able to keep prices low by limiting restaurant commissions, eliminating additional charges, optimising delivery routes through shorter last-mile distances, batching orders, and leveraging its existing logistics and customer support infrastructure. According to the company, these structural efficiencies improve delivery density and operating leverage as order volumes increase, while allowing it to offer lower prices without relying on deep discounts. Swiggy expects affordability-led initiatives such as Toing to help its food delivery business grow at 25%-30% annually, with the segment’s GOV projected to increase 2.5X-3.
paragraph5: 5X by FY31. On the quick commerce front, Swiggy said Instamart’s contribution margin breakeven in Q1 FY27 marked an important milestone in its path towards long-term profitability. The company expects the business to continue scaling rapidly over the next five years while benefiting from higher operating leverage.

title: OpenAI says Apple’s trade secrets lawsuit is ‘rotten to its core’
title_bn: OpenAI says Apple’s trade secrets lawsuit is ‘rotten to its core’
author: TechPulse
excerpt: OpenAI has asked a federal judge to toss out Apple's landmark lawsuit accusing the ChatGPT maker of stealing trade secrets, describing the allegations as "meritless." In a motion filed yesterday to dismiss the complaint, OpenAI says that Apple is mis
paragraph1: Jess Weatherbed is a news writer focused on creative industries, computing, and internet culture. Jess started her career at TechRadar, covering news and hardware reviews.OpenAI has asked a federal judge to toss out Apple’s landmark lawsuit accusing the ChatGPT maker of stealing trade secrets, describing the allegations as “meritless.
paragraph2: ” In a motion filed yesterday to dismiss the complaint, OpenAI says that Apple is mischaracterizing both the actions of the AI startup’s employees as theft, and “generic” product development information as “trade secrets,” adding that Apple made no reasonable efforts to maintain such secrecy.The dismissal request is in response to a lawsuit filed by Apple in July, alleging that former Apple employees that went on to work for OpenAI stole confidential documents to further OpenAI’s hardware development plans. OpenAI’s official legal rebuttal follows a blog post it published on Tuesday titled “Apple is getting this wrong,” in which it described the lawsuit as “careless, aggressive, and oddly personal.
paragraph3: ”Several aspects of that blog make a more formal appearance in OpenAI’s dismissal request, alleging that Apple’s case is poorly investigated, built on selective or out-of-context communications, and “rotten to its core.” For example, OpenAI claims that Chang Liu — a former Apple staffer now working for OpenAI who stands accused of downloading confidential files from Apple after leaving the company — was simply assisting ex-colleagues who asked him for help.“Apple should not be permitted to use a baseless and pretextual lawsuit to make up for its shortcomings in the market for talent and retaining its employees, and its failures to integrate AI into its products,” OpenAI says in the dismissal filing.
paragraph4: “OpenAI is building something entirely new and different from anything at Apple. OpenAI does have an interest in hiring the best engineers, inventors, developers and creators — many of whom have decided to leave Apple and to come to OpenAI, attracted by the innovative and exciting work the company is doing.”The judge is set to hear arguments on the motion on October 1st.
paragraph5: Meanwhile, Apple also asked for a preliminary injunction on Monday to prevent OpenAI and the employees named in the complaint from accessing, acquiring, using, or disclosing alleged confidential information while the lawsuit moves ahead.Follow topics and authors from this story to see more like this in your personalized homepage feed and to receive email updates.

title: Consint.AI Bags ₹22 Cr To Expand Globally, Build AI Model For Risk And Fraud Detection
title_bn: Consint.AI Bags ₹22 Cr To Expand Globally, Build AI Model For Risk And Fraud Detection
author: TechPulse
excerpt: AI startup Consint.AI, which offers an AI-powered healthcare fraud and management platform to enterprises, has raised ₹22 Cr (about $2.3…
paragraph1: SUMMARYConsint.AI has raised ₹22 Cr in a Series A round to scale its AI-powered healthcare and insurance automation platform globally The funding underscores growing investor confidence in vertical AI startups building specialised models for fraud detection, claims processing and enterprise automation in regulated sectors The startup will use the capital to expand across India, the US, the Middle East, Africa and Southeast Asia, while building a foundational AI model for fraud, waste and abuse detection across healthcare, insurance and BFSI AI startup Consint.AI, which offers an AI-powered healthcare fraud and management platform to enterprises, has raised ₹22 Cr (about $2.3 Mn) in its Series A funding round from BIG Global Investment JSC, Equanimity Ventures Trust II, and Seafund Venture India Scheme I. The startup intends to utilise the fresh funds to expand into global markets like the US, MENA, and Southeast Asia.
paragraph2: It will also enhance its AI research in fraud detection and claim processing as well as clinical intelligence. The funds will help the Delhi NCR-based startup develop a foundational model that caters to fraud, waste and abuse (FWA) detection across the insurance, banking and financial services industry. The model will power the startup’s flagship platforms Risk.ai and CIPHR.ai, which aid healthcare providers, insurers, and enterprises in automating processes.
paragraph3: Risk.AI identifies fraudulent transactions and assess underwriting risks and CIPHR AI standardises structured and unstructured patient health records to support clinical workflows and population health analytics. It also has other proprietary platforms, including AutoClaim AI, which is an automated claims processing platform that evaluates insurance claims against policy rules and clinical guidelines. It also offers DocInsight AI, an AI-powered document intelligence platform that digitises and classifies documents using OCR and natural language processing. Founded in 2020 by Ashish Chaturvedi, Swadeep Singh and Rajat Shah, the startup offers a suite of AI products designed to automate claims processing, detect fraud, digitise documents and standardise healthcare records.
paragraph4: The startup primarily targets insurers, hospitals and financial institutions looking to automate high-volume operational workflows while improving compliance and fraud detection. Consint claims to have assessed over 100 Mn transactions on its platform and identified over ₹1,000 Cr in fraud using its AI/ML models and digitised clinical protocols. Consint.AI had earlier raised ₹5 Cr in a seed round in 2025 from Equanimity Ventures and Seafund. With the latest infusion, the startup’s total funding rose to over ₹27 Cr.
paragraph5: It operates in the increasingly crowded enterprise AI segment focused on healthcare, insurance and BFSI automation, where startups are using AI to streamline claims processing, fraud detection, underwriting and document intelligence. Apart from global incumbents, India’s startup ecosystem has also seen a wave of specialised players building vertical AI solutions. For instance, Jivi is applying generative AI to clinical workflows and patient care, while Pype AI is developing AI voice agents for healthcare providers, highlighting investor appetite for domain-specific enterprise AI platforms.

For instance, Jivi is applying generative AI to clinical workflows and patient care, while Pype AI is developing AI voice agents for healthcare providers, highlighting investor appetite for domain-specific enterprise AI platforms.

title: One year of updates couldn’t save the Pixel 10’s GPU — and now the Pixel 11 is at risk
title_bn: One year of updates couldn’t save the Pixel 10’s GPU — and now the Pixel 11 is at risk
author: TechPulse
excerpt: What's the state of play with Android 17 on the Pixel 10?
paragraph1: Robert Triggs / Android AuthorityThe Pixel 10 series may be Google’s best phones yet, but gamers got the short end of the stick. The Tensor G5 marked Google’s switch away from Arm’s Mali GPUs in favor of Imagination Technologies’ PowerVR architecture — specifically the mid-range, already aging DXT-48-1536.With the Pixel 11 launch approaching, one question keeps nagging at me: will history repeat itself? Rumors suggest the Tensor G6 will use another modest PowerVR GPU, the CXTP-48-1536. If Google’s recent trajectory is anything to go by, the Pixel 11 could fall even further behind rival flagship GPUs.That’s hardly encouraging for anyone who takes mobile gaming seriously. My biggest concern isn’t peak performance, though. We all know that Google is far more invested in AI silicon and camera processing capabilities when it comes to picking its priorities. Instead, what I’m anxious about is whether Google has ironed out issues that dogged its transition to PowerVR series GPUs almost one year ago.Are you happy with the Pixel 10's gaming performance in August 2026?8 votesA troubled start to a new GPU Rewind to the launch of the Pixel 10 series, and gaming was a mixed bag. General performance wasn’t as bad as many feared. Games like PUBG Mobile, COD Mobile, Genshin Impact, Honkai: Star Rail, and Diablo Immortal were all perfectly playable.
paragraph2: It never descended into the chaos of Samsung Eynos’s AMD Xclipse debut, where some games barely ran at all.However, my early experience was far from issue-free. I noticed antialiasing glitches while playing COD Mobile’s Battle Royale mode at higher graphics settings, causing foliage to flicker in and out of existence. Perhaps more alarming was that performance on some of Android’s best-maintained emulators went from reasonably smooth to outright unplayable. The difference was stark. My Pixel 9 Pro XL maintained near-locked 60 fps in Dolphin’s F-Zero GX. The Pixel 10 Pro XL bounced between 40 and 60fps, with frequent drops below 30fps.The Pixel 10 launched with GPU drivers that simply weren't ready.Even switching to Vulkan, often the faster graphics backend, failed to deliver comparable performance with its last-gen sibling. In fact, enabling anti-aliasing under OpenGL crashed F-Zero GX on launch, while Vulkan produced missing textures when AA was enabled. Neither was an issue with my Pixel 9 Pro XL, pointing to some rather severe issues with early PowerVR drivers.Combined with more aggressive performance throttling than its predecessor, the early impressions of the Pixel 10 series were really quite disappointing.Have Google’s updates fixed the issues?
paragraph3: Robert Triggs / Android AuthorityOf course, unforeseen bugs are somewhat expected when making a major architectural shift like this. As such, Google issued a key driver update for the Pixel 10 series as part of its QPR beta updates around the end of 2025 that certainly improved performance and fixed a few issues in my subsequent testing. Progress on mainstream consumer releases was obviously slower, and the fixes have continued to trickle in over the past few months. Google was spotted fixing various graphics bugs and issues as recently as its March security update, and that work continued with the build-up to Android 17 as well.Now that Google’s latest OS version is rolling out nearly a year after launch, is gaming finally in a good spot for the Pixel 10 series, and does that bode well or poorly for the Pixel 11 range? I retested my usual gaming lineup on a Pixel 10 Pro XL running Android 17 with the July security patch to see how much had changed.The results are encouraging but still not entirely convincing. Graphical glitches seem to be a thing of the past, at least in the popular titles I tested. Most Android games now run smoothly, as long as you’re willing to dial back graphics settings. Even six-year-old Genshin Impact still struggles to hold 60fps at maximum settings, hovering closer to the mid-40s on my most recent playthrough.Software updates can only do so much. Tensor still trails Snapdragon and Exynos in GPU performance, with lower graphics presets and frame-rate caps in games like Asphalt Legends and COD Mobile. I expect the Pixel 11 to remain a capable mid-tier gaming phone, but not a flagship built for the next five years of increasingly demanding Android games and emulators.
paragraph4: Performance is better with Android 17, but far from flawless.Unfortunately, emulator performance remains more of a mixed bag. OpenGL performance in Dolphin is still a mess compared to the Pixel 9’s Mali GPU — the PowerVR graphics unit doesn’t come close to hitting the same 60fps target. Vulkan performance has improved dramatically since launch, but even so, Dolphin’s performance still lags well behind the Pixel 9’s Mali GPU and can’t quite deliver a consistently smooth 60fps. That said, Vulkan performed far worse in NetherSX2, with neither API producing a playable frame rate in Need for Speed: Most Wanted.The Pixel 11 won’t be the gamer’s choiceStephen Headrick / Android AuthorityA year of updates has made the Tensor G5’s PowerVR GPU far more usable than it was at launch. The glitches are largely gone, performance has improved, and the Pixel 10 Pro XL is unquestionably a better gaming phone today than it was a year ago.But that progress doesn’t erase the underlying problem. The phone still has issues and sometimes performs worse than my Pixel 9 Pro XL, particularly when running emulators. Arm’s Mali GPUs benefit from years of mature Vulkan driver development, often allowing them to outperform what their raw specifications suggest. The same clearly can’t be said for Imagination Technologies’ PowerVR DXT series, which, although improved, remains a small but noticeable step backward compared to Google’s 2024 launch. Given the popularity of playing retro classics on Android these days, the Pixel 10 still has a glaring weakness.I'm not convinced Google has learned lessons in time for the Pixel 11's launch.
paragraph5: With that in mind, I’m still incredibly anxious about the upcoming Pixel 11 series. Not only because the Pixel 10 still has a few lingering issues, but also because Google is apparently downgrading to yet another GPU series, the PowerVR CXT range. On paper, the CXT family sits below DXT in Imagination’s product stack, raising obvious questions about performance. However, the “P” model revision that Google is apparently using boasts improved energy efficiency, which, combined with more efficient manufacturing, might surprise us with boosted clock speeds. In any case, I’m not expecting the Tensor G6 to surpass the G5’s DXT cores, which is a disappointing place to start from.My biggest concern isn’t raw performance — it’s drivers. A new GPU architecture means another fresh software stack, and we’ve already seen how painful that transition can be. Hopefully, Google has spent the past year preparing the Pixel 11 instead of simply patching the Pixel 10 after the fact. Its track record doesn’t give me much confidenceIf it takes another year for the Pixel 11 to become a genuinely good gaming phone, I’ll struggle to believe Google is serious about delivering a flagship gaming experience. Prove me wrong, Google.FollowThank you for being part of our community. Read our Comment Policy before posting.

title: Samsung confirms minor setback for Galaxy S26 One UI 9 beta
title_bn: Samsung confirms minor setback for Galaxy S26 One UI 9 beta
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Samsung has delayed One UI 9 beta 5 for the S26 series until next week for "final reviews and quality improvements."
paragraph1: Paul Jones / Android AuthorityTL;DR Samsung has pushed the fifth One UI 9 beta 5 update for the Galaxy S26 series to next week. The delay is due to final reviews and quality improvements to enhance system stability and fix bugs before a stable release. The over-the-air update will roll out to enrolled Galaxy S26, S26 Plus, and S26 Ultra devices in the US, UK, India, Germany, Poland, and South Korea when it goes live next week.
paragraph2: Samsung has confirmed a short delay for the fifth beta build of One UI 9 for the Galaxy S26 series, pushing its expected release into next week. Galaxy S26 owners participating in the preview program will have to hold on a bit longer, following the rollout of the One UI 9 beta 4 update last month.According to an official announcement post on the Samsung Community forum (via Tarun Vats on X), the development team is taking additional time for “final reviews and quality improvements” before rolling out the fifth iteration.
paragraph3: Samsung apologized to community members for the slight delay, citing the need to deliver a more stable, polished software experience to testers.While Samsung did not detail specific bug fixes or feature additions coming with Beta 5, beta builds at this stage typically focus on improving system stability and squashing remaining bugs ahead of a stable public release.The upcoming fifth beta build will be available for enrolled Galaxy S26, S26 Plus, and S26 Ultra devices in the US, UK, India, Germany, Poland, and South Korea.
paragraph4: Users currently enrolled in the One UI 9 beta program can expect an over-the-air update once the build officially goes live next week.FollowThank you for being part of our community. Read our Comment Policy before posting.

title: Galaxy S26 FE appears at FCC with an unexpected Qualcomm twist
title_bn: Galaxy S26 FE appears at FCC with an unexpected Qualcomm twist
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Qualcomm and Exynos silicon in the same phone? Yep, but perhaps not in the way you're expecting.
paragraph1: C. Scott Brown / Android AuthorityTL;DR We’ve uncovered the Samsung Galaxy S26 FE’s FCC filing, revealing 45W charging, reverse wireless charging, and more. The filing also mentions both Qualcomm and Samsung Exynos wireless technologies. A closer look suggests that the phone will have a Samsung modem and chipset, as well as a Qualcomm local networking chip. Samsung has just launched its new foldable phones, but we’re already looking forward to the Galaxy S26 FE‘s imminent arrival. The phone is expected to launch in the coming weeks, and a regulatory filing has revealed a few details.
paragraph2: The Galaxy S26 FE passed through the FCC’s database, and the filing reveals a few notable features. For one, the listing hints at both Qualcomm and Samsung Exynos silicon in the same model. Wait, what?FCCThis filing notes that the Galaxy S26 FE is equipped with both S.LSI (Samsung LSI) and Qualcomm FastConnect technologies for RF transmission. So what does this actually mean, then?
paragraph3: Does this mean the phone will have Exynos or Snapdragon chips, depending on the region?Further reading shows that the phone uses S.LSI technologies for cellular or WWAN functionality, but switches to Qualcomm FastConnect technologies for WLAN functionality (i.e., Wi-Fi). Furthermore, FastConnect refers to Qualcomm’s local wireless networking suite rather than its modems or SoCs.
paragraph4: Devices with Qualcomm modems are usually listed as using “Smart Transmit” functionality rather than FastConnect tech, but we don’t see any “Smart Transmit” references in this filing.This discovery strongly suggests that the Galaxy S26 FE has an Exynos modem and chipset, but a Qualcomm local networking chip. This differs from the Galaxy S25 FE, which only references Samsung transmission technologies in its FCC filing. We’re not sure why Samsung would take this new approach, but it’s possible that the FastConnect chip was cheaper, smaller, more reliable, or more efficient than its own local networking solution. Either way, it sounds like US buyers might not be getting a Snapdragon variant.FCCThe FCC filing also reveals that the Galaxy S26 FE has 45W wired charging (see image above).
paragraph5: This lines up with a previous regulatory filing and means the FE model once again boasts faster charging speeds than the base flagship.Other specs gleaned from the listing include reverse wireless charging functionality, NFC, Wi-Fi 6 support, and supplemental satellite support akin to T-Mobile‘s direct-to-cell functionality.FollowThank you for being part of our community. Read our Comment Policy before posting.

title: Vivo S2 launched in India with Dimensity 7360 Turbo SoC, 7,050mAh battery: Price, specs and launch offers
title_bn: Vivo S2 launched in India with Dimensity 7360 Turbo SoC, 7,050mAh battery: Price, specs and launch offers
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Vivo has launched the S2 in India, featuring a 120Hz AMOLED display and MediaTek Dimensity 7360 Turbo processor.
paragraph1: Vivo has launched the S2 in India, featuring a 120Hz AMOLED display and MediaTek Dimensity 7360 Turbo processor. Vivo S2Vivo has brought back its S series in India with the Vivo S2. The new mid-range devices comes with a 120Hz AMOLED display, MediaTek's Dimensity 7360 Turbo processor, a 7,050mAh battery with 44W fast charging and an IP68 + IP69 rating.Here's everything you need to know about the Vivo S2.Vivo S2 price in India:The Vivo S2 is priced at Rs. 39,999 for the 8GB + 128GB variant and Rs. 49,999 for the 8GB + 256GB model.As part of the launch offers, Vivo is offering up to 10% instant bank discount with select bank cards, along with up to 10% exchange bonus, bringing down the effective price for eligible buyers. Customers can also avail up to 15 months no-cost EMI and a one-year free extended warranty.Additionally, buyers will get 5,000GB of Jio Cloud storage for 18 months along with complimentary access to Google Gemini Pro.
paragraph2: The Vivo S2 will go on sale starting 11 August via the Vivo India e-store, Flipkart, Amazon and retail stores across the country.Vivo S2 specificationsThe Vivo S2 sports a 6.83-inch 1.5K AMOLED display with a 120Hz refresh rate, HDR10+ support and 4,320Hz PWM dimming. The phone also comes with IP68 and IP69 ratings for dust and water resistance.Under the hood, the Vivo S2 is powered by MediaTek's Dimensity 7360 Turbo processor. It comes with 8GB or 12GB of LPDDR4X RAM and up to 512GB of UFS 3.1 storage.The Vivo S2 runs on OriginOS 6 based on Android 16 with a promise of 3 years of OS updates and 5 years of security patches. The Vivo S2 packs a 7,050mAh battery with support for 44W fast charging.
paragraph3: For optics, the smartphone features a 50-megapixel primary camera paired with a 2-megapixel depth sensor. On the front, it houses a 32-megapixel selfie camera. Both the front and rear cameras support 4K video recording.In terms of connectivity, the smartphone comes with support for 5G, dual 4G VoLTE, Wi-Fi 6, Bluetooth 5.4, GPS, BeiDou, GLONASS, Galileo, QZSS and a USB Type-C port. The Vivo S2 also features an in-display optical fingerprint scanner, infrared sensor and stereo speakers.FeatureSpecificationDisplay6.83-inch 1.5K AMOLED (1260 × 2800 pixels), 120Hz refresh rate, HDR10+, 4,320Hz PWM dimmingProcessorMediaTek Dimensity 7360 Turbo (4nm)RAM8GB / 12GB LPDDR4XStorage256GB / 512GB UFS 3.1SoftwareAndroid 16 with OriginOS 6Rear camera50MP primary + 2MP depthFront camera32MPBattery7,050mAhCharging44W fast chargingSecurityIn-display optical fingerprint sensorDurabilityIP68 + IP69 dust and water resistanceAudioStereo speakers, USB Type-C audioConnectivity5G, Dual 4G VoLTE, Wi-Fi 6, Bluetooth 5.

title: Meet the photonics scaleups building tomorrow's critical technologies
title_bn: Meet the photonics scaleups building tomorrow's critical technologies
author: TechPulse
excerpt: From faster internet and more secure satellite communications to next-generation semiconductors, quantum technologies and energy-generating greenhouses, photonics is becoming one of Europe's most stra...
paragraph1: From faster internet and more secure satellite communications to next-generation semiconductors, quantum technologies and energy-generating greenhouses, photonics is becoming one of Europe's most strategically important deep tech sectors. Europe is home to a new generation of photonics scaleups translating decades of scientific research into commercially viable products. By generating, transmitting and manipulating light, photonic technologies deliver higher performance while reducing the size, weight, power consumption and cost of complex systems. As demand for AI infrastructure, high-performance computing and resilient digital networks continues to grow, photonics is emerging as a foundational technology for the next generation of innovation, strengthening Europe's technological sovereignty and creating globally competitive businesses. Here are some companies to have on your radar: EFFECT Photonics (Netherlands) EFFECT Photonics develops integrated photonic semiconductor chips and optical communication systems that enable faster, lower-cost, and lower-power data transmission across telecom and data centre networks. Its technology integrates multiple optical functions—including lasers, modulators, photodetectors and digital signal processing—onto a single chip, reducing the size, cost and complexity of optical networking equipment. Image: EFFECT Photonics.
paragraph2: Cailabs (France) Cailabs develops advanced photonic systems that control and shape laser light. The company's core technology is Multi-Plane Light Conversion (MPLC), a proprietary beam-shaping technology that precisely manipulates laser light. This enables more reliable, higher-capacity optical communications and more precise industrial laser applications. Its solutions include optical ground stations and laser communication systems for satellites, beam-shaping technologies for defence applications, photonic components that boost the capacity and reliability of fibre-optic networks, and optical systems that improve the precision and efficiency of industrial laser welding, cutting and additive manufacturing. Wooptix (Spain) Wooptix develops advanced optical metrology equipment for the semiconductor industry, helping chip manufacturers measure and inspect silicon wafers with extremely high precision. At the core of Wooptix's products is its proprietary Wavefront Phase Imaging (WFPI) technology, derived from adaptive optics originally developed for astronomy. The technology analyses how light changes as it passes through or reflects from a surface, enabling single-shot measurements of wafer shape, nanotopography and surface roughness with exceptionally high resolution and speed.
paragraph3: This allows semiconductor manufacturers to improve process control, increase manufacturing yields and support increasingly complex chip architectures such as advanced packaging and 3D integration. Mbryonics (Ireland) Mbryonics develops advanced optical communications technologies for the space sector, designing optical terminals, laser communication payloads and photonic integrated circuits that enable satellites to transmit far greater volumes of data than traditional radio-frequency systems. Its free-space optical communication technology uses lasers instead of radio waves to create secure, high-bandwidth links between satellites and from space to Earth for applications including satellite constellations, Earth observation and deep-space missions. The company specialises in integrated photonics, combining optical components onto compact semiconductor chips to reduce the size, weight and power requirements of satellite communications equipment. Its integrated photonics platform also improves the performance, manufacturability and cost efficiency of optical systems. Quside (Spain) Quside develops quantum tech that enhances cybersecurity, high-performance computing and scientific research through the generation and manipulation of quantum light. The company's core products are quantum random number generators (QRNGs), which use the inherent unpredictability of quantum physics to produce truly random numbers.
paragraph4: These provide a higher level of security than conventional software-based random number generators and are used in applications including encryption, secure communications, data centres, cloud infrastructure and financial systems. Quside also develops single-photon sources for quantum computing, quantum sensing and quantum communications. Its integrated photonics technology is designed to deliver scalable, compact and energy-efficient quantum hardware. Brite Solar (Greece) Combining photonics, materials science and solar technology, Brite Solar develops transparent photovoltaic glass for greenhouses, allowing growers to generate renewable electricity while maintaining the optimal light conditions for crops. Its patented solar glass uses advanced optical coatings to selectively transmit the wavelengths plants need for photosynthesis while converting the remaining sunlight into electricity. This enables greenhouses to reduce energy costs and carbon emissions without compromising crop growth or yields. Collectively, these scale-ups highlight Europe's strength in photonics, transforming advances in light-based technologies into commercial products that address some of today's most pressing technological and industrial challenges.
paragraph5: Companies mentioned in this article are members of the EIC Scaling Club, a curated community where 120+ European deep tech scale-ups with the potential to build world-class businesses and solve major global challenges come together with investors, corporate innovators and other industry stakeholders to spur growth. The EIC Scaling Club is an EIC-funded initiative run in partnership with Tech Tour, Bpifrance (EuroQuity), Hello Tomorrow, Tech.eu (Webrazzi), EurA and IESE Business School.

title: As a daily Android Auto user, these are the 5 features I still want after the big 2026 update
title_bn: As a daily Android Auto user, these are the 5 features I still want after the big 2026 update
author: TechPulse
excerpt: 3D navigation, video support, and widgets are nice, but here's what Android Auto actually needs.
paragraph1: Andy Walker / Android AuthoritySignificant updates are coming to Android Auto this year, and some features have already appeared on the dashboards of a few lucky users. Google’s new offerings include immersive 3D navigation in Google Maps, video playback support for YouTube users, and home screen widget support, with more features in the pipeline.It’s a substantial list of new additions, but as consumers are never quite satisfied, there’s always room for further improvement.Beyond the many welcome features arriving in 2026, here are a few improvements that Android Auto desperately needs, could benefit from, or would make a pleasant addition to the driving experience.What feature do you want to see most on Android Auto?9 votesGemini via Android Auto sucks – here’s how Google can fix itRita El Khoury / Android AuthorityI’m generally fond of Gemini’s sparkly presence, especially when it corrects my error-laden spreadsheets or polishes my rambling emails to fellow adults. It’s a different story entirely when it comes to the in-car voice-prompting experience.Android Auto’s iteration of Gemini is horrible. Not only is it overly chirpy, but it also takes much more time to complete tasks than its simpler, older predecessor. Altering navigation instructions, querying road conditions ahead, requesting the weather conditions, or playing specific playlists from Spotify should be child’s play for the next-generation assistant — but there’s always a delay between my command and its execution.How's your experience with Gemini on Android Auto?338 votesGemini might be unpolished at present, but it’s fixable. Given how well it runs on Android and Wear OS, the in-car experience could be greatly improved with just a few simple additions.
paragraph2: These include: Gemini response settings specifically for Android Auto: At the very least, I’d like toggles to adjust Gemini’s response verbosity, the tone I’d prefer it use, and the circumstances in which it should ask follow-up questions while driving. Gemini Profiles for Android Auto: Take the settings above. Now imagine them placed within specific profiles. These would allow drivers to set up specific response setting combinations for specific driving situations. For example, a “work” profile could make Gemini more direct for morning commutes. A “weekend” profile could be more informative and conversational. A “kids” profile would be perfect for keeping little ones entertained on long drives. These profiles could be activated and deactivated via a voice command. Saved Info for Android Auto: I love using Saved Info to change my text-based Gemini responses on the web or in the app, but it often affects how it responds to voice queries in the car. A dedicated Saved Info page for Android Auto would allow for even more customization of responses and keep other info siloed to its intended platforms. A “Stop” word: I really need Gemini to just stop when it rambles on in traffic. A stop word, or anti-wake word, would be a welcome kill switch to instantly halt its response. “No, Google,” anyone?
paragraph3: There are plenty of additional improvements to Gemini I’d love to see, including an overall boost to processing and response speed and a more reliable hit rate for obvious, regular commands like “Yes” and “No.”Some of the suggested features below also include Gemini to some degree.Please bring voice messaging to Android AutoSanuj Bhatia / Android AuthorityIt’s 2026, but somehow I still can’t send a voice message to my contacts through Android Auto.Although my car and phone both have microphones, Android Auto forcibly, and often incorrectly, transcribes messages into text instead of simply sending the audio. We can place calls, so why can’t we send recorded voice snippets via WhatsApp or RCS?I’d welcome Android Auto offering me the choice between text and voice messaging for contacts (this preference could be set via a settings toggle), with voice messaging ensuring information is relayed more accurately to recipients. I can’t tell you how often Gemini includes parts of the command in transcribed messages, how often it spells out “full stop” and “comma,” or how often it completely butchers the names of recipients or locations.While Google is working on a voice messaging feature, at least according to Gemini itself, it’s unclear when the feature will actually arrive. It’s certainly a feature I’d like the company to prioritize over widgets and other flashy visual updates.No more contact ambiguity and confusionAdamya Sharma / Android AuthorityAs I mentioned above, Gemini misunderstands what I’m trying to relay in a message. More annoyingly, it’s often confused by who I’d like to contact. This is especially problematic for names and countries that are not spelled as they’re seemingly pronounced.The Contacts app has a fix just waiting to be better integrated.
paragraph4: Setting Phonetic First Names and Phonetic Last Names, in addition to Nicknames within the app, is possible, and I’d certainly suggest that you fill these fields. However, Android Auto seems to disregard this information whenever I ask it to reach a contact.What's the point of phonetic spellings and nickname fields in Contacts if Gemini disregards them?The fix, which could benefit millions of people, is to have Gemini check these specific contact fields first while driving. This would also stop Gemini from seeking nicknames as if they were first-name contacts.Give me more boring visual toggles!Andy Walker / Android AuthorityGoogle Maps’ new immersive navigation gimmick is impressive, but does it genuinely improve the overall navigation experience? Not quite. What certainly would is the ability to tweak various Maps interface elements to my liking. Google’s been focused on updating Android Auto’s design language and aesthetics, but there are more practical items it could hand off to users.As I’ve mentioned in a previous opinion piece, Android Auto is a driving tool, and driving tools should allow the driver to customize them to best suit their needs. It’s why a steering wheel has rake adjustments, why seats can be lowered or raised, and why mirrors can be reangled. A comfortable driver is a safer driver.
paragraph5: This focus on accommodation and accessibility should be present in Android Auto, too. Here are some concepts: Additional themes or visual styles for Google Maps: Mapping apps like OsmAnd allow users to enable various map elements, change colors, and adjust typefaces. Google Maps could certainly do with similar legibility and information toggles to improve accessibility. Options to reposition and resize boxes, toggles, buttons, and other elements: Imagine a suite of settings that lets you increase the skip button, thicken the seek bar, enlarge the navigation details box, and much more. Options to revert to previous layouts and UI styles: Not everyone wants Google to revise and shuffle UI elements with every update. This option would allow users to reduce disruption by preferring legacy layouts and interface experiences. A broader power saver mode for Android AutoMishaal Rahman / Android AuthorityAndroid Auto is a battery hog, and my phone often switches into power-saving mode while I’m connected to it.At present, when my phone reaches this battery breaking point, Android Auto continues to function without abandon. To save device power, I’d like to see Android Auto automatically switch to a low-battery mode when my phone does and subsequently trigger additional power-rationing features.The mode could automatically restrict my phone’s network to 3G or 4G, disable transparency and other demanding visual effects, limit the mapping feature to show directions only, and restrict access to a handful of Android Auto-compatible apps. Essentially, such a mode would turn my phone into an Android Auto modem and little else.Android Auto on some vehicles has a power-saving mode, but it's not as widespread or extensive as it could be.

title: Google may finally fix a major frustration with Android’s Photo Picker
title_bn: Google may finally fix a major frustration with Android’s Photo Picker
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Code in Android 17 QPR 2 Beta 2 reveals plans for a built-in media editor, which could save users from tedious app switching.
paragraph1: Mishaal Rahman / Android AuthorityTL;DR Google is laying the groundwork to add a built-in media editor directly to the Android Photo Picker. Code in Android 17 QPR2 Beta 2 reveals an “EditFeature” class designed as a pop-up dialog for quick edits like cropping and marking. Because the Photo Picker updates via Google Play System Updates, this feature can roll out independently of a full OS update. Android’s Photo Picker is a system component that provides third-party apps with a browsable interface for accessing media library content. It’s a massive leap forward for user privacy, as it allows users to share specific photos and videos with third-party apps without giving them access to their full media library. For app developers, it saves them the effort of building this interface themselves.
paragraph2: Google has refocused its efforts on improving the Android Photo Picker, as we’ve spotted features like a camera shortcut in the works. You can look forward to another new feature coming soon: a media editor.You’re reading an Authority Insights story. Authority Insights brings you all the latest exclusive reports, app teardowns, leaks, and in-depth tech coverage from the Android Authority team that you won’t find anywhere else.Currently, if you are using apps that integrate the Android Photo Picker, you can select existing media to share with the app.However, if during the selection process, you realize you want to make any edits to the media, say cropping it in a certain aspect ratio before sending, you will have to exit the Photo Picker, minimize the third-party app, navigate to the media gallery app on your phone, make edits to your media and ensure you save the edits, minimize/exit the gallery app, return to the third-party app, and resume sending through the Android Photo Picker.
paragraph3: As you can imagine, this is tedious and full of unnecessary friction.Code in Android 17 QPR 2 Beta 2 suggests that Google is laying the groundwork to add a media editor to the Android Photo Picker. We’ve spotted a new class aptly named “EditFeature,” which seemingly integrates directly into the Photo Picker as a pop-up dialog. Other clues in the code corroborate that this feature is related to image editing functionality built directly into the Android Photo Picker.AssembleDebug / Android AuthorityOnce this change goes live, users may potentially be able to make simple edits, such as cropping or marking media, directly in the Photo Picker, saving them from having to minimize the third-party app and navigate to a media gallery app.This would remove friction for the user and, for the app developer, reduce opportunities for users to exit the app and remove the need to build a media-editing interface for simple edits.
paragraph4: Users will also get a consistent editing experience across third-party apps that integrate the Android Photo Picker, which is a big win in making the OS feel cohesive.The Android Photo Picker is a Project Mainline module and is updated through Google Play System Updates. As such, Google can roll out the feature independent of an OS update. We couldn’t activate the feature just yet, suggesting that Google still has some work to do in the background before it’s ready for rollout. We’ll keep you updated when we learn more.⚠️ An APK teardown helps predict features that may arrive on a service in the future based on work-in-progress code.
paragraph5: However, it is possible that such predicted features may not make it to a public release.FollowThank you for being part of our community. Read our Comment Policy before posting.

title: Piper Serica’s ₹800 Cr Bharat Tech Fund Hits First Close At ₹300 Cr
title_bn: Piper Serica’s ₹800 Cr Bharat Tech Fund Hits First Close At ₹300 Cr
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Mumbai-based asset management firm Piper Serica has achieved the first close of its ₹800 Cr Bharat Tech Fund at ₹300…
paragraph1: SUMMARYPiper Serica’s ₹800 Cr Bharat Tech Fund has achieved its first close at ₹300 Cr The fundraise highlights rising investor interest in India’s deeptech ecosystem as advanced technology startups gain traction Nearly 50% of commitments came from existing investors, with the fund targeting ₹20-₹50 Cr investments per startup Mumbai-based asset management firm Piper Serica has achieved the first close of its ₹800 Cr Bharat Tech Fund at ₹300 Cr. The development comes months after Piper Serica launched the Category II AIF with a target corpus of ₹600 Cr and a ₹200 Cr greenshoe option. The fund will back Series A and Series B deeptech startups across deeptech sectors, including semiconductors, AI, spacetech, defence tech, biosciences, and fintech infrastructure. Piper Serica plans to invest between ₹20 Cr and ₹50 Cr in each startup and is targeting a gross internal rate of return (IRR) of about 30% over an average holding period of six years. Nearly 50% of the commitments for the fund have come from existing investors in Piper Serica’s first venture fund.
paragraph2: Piper Serica Bets On India’s Deeptech Opportunity According to Piper Serica, it is seeing a strong pipeline of deeptech startups that are moving beyond early-stage product development and building revenue-generating businesses. The firm’s first venture fund backed startups including Alt Mobility, Pantherun, Rupeeflo, OTPless, Yaanendriya, Vobiz, and Six Sense Mobility. Founded in 2003 by Abhay Agarwal, Piper Serica invests across public markets and early-stage startups. Its first venture fund, Piper Serica Angel Fund, was launched in 2022 with a target corpus of ₹100 Cr and has made 35 investments across sectors such as semiconductors, AI and spacetech. The firm backed startups including Mysa, Sensesemi Technologies and Vobiz in the first quarter of 2026.
paragraph3: It also recently invested $1 Mn in airport operations technology startup Blunav. Piper Serica initially planned to complete the final close of the Bharat Tech Fund by December 2026 but now expects to close the fund ahead of schedule. The fundraise comes at a time when investor interest in India’s deeptech sector is gaining momentum, with startups working on AI, semiconductors, spacetech and defence technologies drawing increased attention. The trend is visible in the rise of new funds targeting the space. Recently, Groww’s cofounders were said to be planning a second fund with a corpus of ₹400-500 Cr for seed and early-stage startups.
paragraph4: AUM Ventures also launched its India Innovation Fund II with a ₹750 Cr target corpus to back startups across deeptech segments. Government support has also played a role in strengthening the ecosystem. The Centre has extended Startup India benefits for deeptech startups to 20 years and raised the turnover eligibility limit for related schemes to ₹300 Cr from ₹200 Cr. The Centre’s push has further expanded with the India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) 2.0, backed by a ₹1.
paragraph5: 27 lakh Cr outlay to support the semiconductor value chain, including chip design, equipment and advanced manufacturing.

title: Netflix Launches India Creator Initiative As Ted Sarandos Bets Big On Local Content, AI
title_bn: Netflix Launches India Creator Initiative As Ted Sarandos Bets Big On Local Content, AI
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Netflix has launched the Netflix India Storytelling Initiative, a new programme aimed at training and supporting creators across animation, visual…
paragraph1: SUMMARYNetflix has launched the Netflix India Storytelling Initiative to build a pipeline of creators across AVGC, partnering with IICT and NFDC for training programmes The initiative builds on Netflix’s decade-long presence in India, with the company creating more than 200 originals and filming across over 100 locations Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos said India is central to the company's global strategy, highlighted AI's growing role in entertainment production, and ruled out bidding for major sports rights such as the IPL Netflix has launched the Netflix India Storytelling Initiative, a new programme aimed at training and supporting creators across animation, visual effects, gaming and comics (AVGC), as the streaming giant deepens its long-term investment in India. Under the initiative, Netflix will partner with the Indian Institute of Creative Technologies (IICT) and the National Film Development Corporation (NFDC) to train young talent for the entertainment industry. Through its partnership with NFDC, Netflix will also support training for accessibility roles, including audio description writers and voice professionals, to make Indian films and series more accessible. The programme builds on Netflix’s decade-long presence in India, during which it has produced more than 200 originals and filmed across more than 100 locations. The announcement comes amid Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos’s India visit. Yesterday, Sarandos met Prime Minister Narendra Modi and discussed India’s growing influence in global entertainment and the potential of its media sector, ANI reported.
paragraph2: Sarandos was accompanied by Netflix’s India head Monika Shergill. India Central To Netflix’s Growth Plans India is emerging as one of Netflix’s most important growth markets as the company looks to expand its global subscriber base. In an interview with The Economic Times, Sarandos said Netflix has an estimated 20-25 Mn paid subscribers in India, compared with its global subscriber base of more than 325 Mn. “There could be no Netflix globally without India. You can’t be successful without it,” Sarandos said. He said India’s large entertainment audience, diverse creator ecosystem, rising smartphone and connected TV adoption, and affordable internet access make it a critical market for the streaming platform.
paragraph3: However, Sarandos added that India cannot be treated as a single market, given its linguistic and cultural diversity, requiring Netflix to invest across multiple genres, languages and formats. Notably, Netflix’s India strategy has evolved over the years. While the company initially focused on premium scripted content with shows such as Sacred Games, it later expanded into reality and unscripted programming. Sarandos cited shows such as Lock Upp and The Great Indian Kapil Show as examples of Netflix broadening its content portfolio. He added that Indian consumers are “value-conscious, not just price-conscious”, and are willing to pay for platforms that consistently deliver compelling content. Netflix’s mobile-only subscription plan was first piloted in India before being rolled out in other markets.
paragraph4: On sports streaming, Sarandos said Netflix is unlikely to compete for full-season rights such as the Indian Premier League (IPL), preferring instead to focus on selective live events and special-format programming. While Netflix does not disclose country-level profitability, Sarandos said the company is satisfied with the economics of its India business. He added that Netflix has not pursued a “loss leader” strategy to acquire market share, instead focusing on delivering enough value for users to retain their subscriptions. “We want to be the first place you check and the last service you cancel,” Sarandos told ET. AI To Reshape Entertainment Production Sarandos also described AI as a transformative force for the entertainment industry, comparing its impact with the shift from hand-drawn animation to computer-generated animation. According to ET, Netflix is already using AI across pre-visualisation, production planning, visual effects and post-production workflows.
paragraph5: Sarandos said AI could lower the cost of advanced filmmaking techniques, including digital de-ageing of actors, making such technologies more accessible to creators. Addressing concerns over job losses, he said previous technological shifts had ultimately created new opportunities across the entertainment industry. On the launch of Netflix’s advertising-supported subscription plan in India, Sarandos said the company plans to introduce it eventually but is “not there yet”.

title: [Update] Exclusive: HomeRun Raises $12 Mn To Scale Construction Materials Quick Commerce Platform
title_bn: [Update] Exclusive: HomeRun Raises $12 Mn To Scale Construction Materials Quick Commerce Platform
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Update | August 6, 2026, 10:15 IST Quick commerce startup for construction and interior materials HomeRun has raised $12 Mn…
paragraph1: SUMMARYHomeRun is in talks to raise around ₹100 Cr (about $11 Mn), people aware of the matter told Inc42 on the condition of anonymity. As per sources, the fresh round is likely to be led by Nexus Venture Partners with participation from HomeRun’s existing investors including Sorin Investments, among others The startup’s post money valuation is likely to be between ₹450 Cr - ₹500 Cr. Update | August 6, 2026, 10:15 IST Quick commerce startup for construction and interior materials HomeRun has raised $12 Mn (about ₹114 Cr) in a Series A+ funding round led by Nexus Venture Partners. The round also saw participation from existing investors Sorin Investments, Titan Capital, Sparrow Capital, and Consumer Collective by Atrium. The startup said that the fresh capital will be used to expand into new geographies and invest further in supply chain, technology and category expansion. HomeRun said it has delivered more than 1 Lakh orders and grew its business 8X over the past 12 months, making it the largest retailer in Bengaluru across its top product categories.
paragraph2: The development comes months after Inc42 exclusively reported that the startup was in talks to raise around ₹100 Cr. Original| March 10, 2026, 15:30 IST Bengaluru-based quick commerce for construction and home improvement materials startup HomeRun is in talks to raise around ₹100 Cr (about $11 Mn), people aware of the matter told Inc42 on the condition of anonymity. As per sources, the fresh round is likely to be led by Nexus Venture Partners with participation from HomeRun’s existing investors including Sorin Investments, among others. The startup’s post money valuation is likely to be between ₹450 Cr – ₹500 Cr. It is pertinent to note that the size and valuation of the round are yet to be finalised and can see some variations in the coming days. Questions sent to HomeRun and Nexus Venture Partners didn’t elicit any response at the time of publication.
paragraph3: The fresh development comes almost a month after the startup announced a $6.6 Mn in a funding round led by Sorin Investments. Other investors like Titan Capital Winners Fund, Sparrow Capital, Consumer Collective by Atrium, and Helios Holdings also joined the startup’s cap table back then. Founded in 2024 by Pukhraj Grewal, HomeRun claims to deliver construction and renovation materials within 60 to 90 mins. The startup’s SKUs include cement, tiles, paints, water proofing products, wires, plywood, among others. Currently, the startup’s services are available in Bengaluru.
paragraph4: Prior to setting up HomeRun, Grewal founded construction-focussed labour hiring platform Project Hero in 2021. Although the startup had raised capital from Ankur Capital and Omidyar Network India, it had to shut shop in 2024. With the fresh capital, the startup will expand its operations in newer cities by setting up newer dark stores. After strengthening its presence in Bengaluru, it intends to expand in cities like Hyderabad and Pune. The quick commerce business model has become investors favorite in the last few years. It started with grocery delivery, where investors poured billions of dollars to capture market share.
paragraph5: Swiggy’s Instamart, Eternal’s Blinkit, and Zepto continue to command a lion’s share in this particular space. After seeing success in this space, the quick commerce business model later went vertical, by catering into niche segments such as house help, quick food, child care, and now even beauty. Just last week, quick maid services platform Pronto bagged $25 Mn in funding at a $100 Mn valuation. Its competitor Snabbit is in talks to raise $100 Mn – $125 Mn in funding.

paragraph1: SUMMARYShiprocket has filed its RHP to ₹1,617 Cr via its IPO, a 30% reduction from the ₹2,342.3 Cr proposed in its updated DRHP. The issue reflects how new-age tech companies are recalibrating fundraising strategies to align with prevailing public market conditions and investor expectations. The IPO comprises a fresh issue of equity shares worth up to ₹885.5 Cr and an offer for sale (OFS) aggregating up to ₹732 Cr. Logistics major shiprocket has filed the RHP to raise ₹1,617 Cr (about $170 Mn) via its IPO, a 30% reduction from the ₹2,342.3 Cr proposed in its updated DRHP. The issue will open for subscription on August 12 and close on August 14.
paragraph2: The company has fixed a price band of ₹92-97 per equity share for the public issue, valuing the company at around ₹7,000 Cr (about $736 Mn). The IPO comprises a fresh issue of equity shares worth up to ₹885.5 Cr and an offer for sale (OFS) aggregating up to ₹732 Cr. In comparison, the company’s UDRHP had proposed a fresh issue of ₹1,100 Cr and an OFS of about ₹1,242 Cr. Cofounders Saahil Goel, Gautam Kapoor, and Vishesh Khurana will pare their stakes as part of the OFS. Goel and Kapoor will offload shares worth ₹61 Cr each, while Khurana will sell shares worth ₹20 Cr. Among institutional investors, PE firm Lightrock will be the biggest seller in the OFS, offloading shares worth about ₹272 Cr. Silicon Valley-based Tribe Capital plans to sell shares worth ₹120 Cr.
paragraph3: Other investors participating in the OFS include March Capital, 500 Global, Agility Global and Moore Strategic Ventures. Notably, Bertelsmann India Investments and Arvind Ltd, which were part of the OFS in the UDRHP, are no longer selling shares. Bertelsmann India Investments is the largest shareholder in the company with a 21.3% stake. Other large shareholders not paring their stakes include Zomato’s parent company Eternal, which owns a 6.85% stake in Shiprocket as of the date of filing the RHP. The Gurugram-based startup plans to use the proceeds from the fresh issue to invest in technology infrastructure, marketing initiatives, potential acquisitions, debt repayment and other general corporate purposes. Founded in 2017 by Goel, Kapoor, Khurana and Akshay Ghulati, Shiprocket started as a logistics aggregation platform and has since expanded into a full-stack ecommerce enablement player, offering services across shipping, warehousing, checkout, payments, marketing and cross-border commerce.
paragraph4: On the financial front, Shiprocket reported a 24% increase in its operating revenue to ₹2,024 Cr in FY26 from ₹1,632 Cr in the previous year. However, its net loss widened over 6% to ₹79.2 Cr during the fiscal from ₹74.5 Cr in FY25. Most of its income was generated through the sale of services, namely merchant solutions, which fetched Shiprocket ₹2,008.1 Cr in FY26, while around ₹16 Cr was earned from the sale of traded goods. Its expenses during the year stood at ₹2,153.4 Cr, up 23% YoY from ₹1,749.
paragraph5: 2 reported in FY25. Notably, a bulk of its expenses went toward the cost of merchant solutions, which rose 23% YoY to ₹1,494.1 Cr. Once listed, Shiprocket will join listed logistics and fulfilment players such as Shadowfax and Delhivery on the bourses. Its IPO comes at a time when new-age tech IPOs have regained momentum, even as several players like Zepto, Flipkart and PhonePe have their public issues on hold.

title: Google Home kicks off August with big app updates and a smarter Gemini for Home
title_bn: Google Home kicks off August with big app updates and a smarter Gemini for Home
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Google Home's first August update is packed with useful new features.
paragraph1: Edgar Cervantes / Android AuthorityTL;DR Google has added an interactive AI Storytime feature to Gemini for Home that lets families create and modify stories using voice commands. The update also improves alarms, timers, and other everyday features while fixing several bugs. The Google Home app now supports more smart camera brands and includes several new camera viewing and recording improvements. Google has announced a fresh batch of updates for Gemini for Home (Early access) and the Google Home app. The latest August 5 update adds a fun new AI-powered Storytime feature to Gemini for Home and promises to make everyday smart home controls more reliable in the app.
paragraph2: One of the biggest additions is a new Interactive Storytime feature for Gemini. It allows users to create and modify stories by issuing voice commands to the AI assistant.You can ask Gemini to invent an original story, put your children into the adventure, or change the plot while the story is being told. For example, you can replace the Big Bad Wolf in The Three Little Pigs with a T. rex or have the main character suddenly discover a treasure map.
paragraph3: Outside of Storytime, Google is also improving some of the features people use every day. Gemini for Home is now smarter and better at understanding alarm and timer requests in natural language, including your preference for a 12-hour or 24-hour clock.Gemini is also getting better at answering questions like how much time is left on a timer, and it can now more reliably understand requests such as setting a timer for cooking a soft-boiled egg.Googe Home app improvements The company has also made a few quality-of-life improvements to Google Home speakers. Turning off or dimming the lights now plays a different confirmation sound, and a bug that could leave the speaker’s light ring glowing after routines finished has been fixed.
paragraph4: Google also notes that a brief Spotify outage from late July has been resolved.Meanwhile, the Google Home app is receiving a much larger update focused on cameras and smart home devices.One of the biggest changes is support for more third-party security cameras, including models from Eufy, Tapo, Wyze, Reolink, and Nanit, allowing users to view more camera feeds from within a single app. Google has also added a quicker way to save camera recordings, improved live streaming reliability, made camera views easier to navigate, and introduced several Android- and iOS-specific performance improvements.Subscribers to Home Premium Advanced also get AI-generated summaries of camera events, making it easier to understand what happened without watching the entire recording.
paragraph5: Finally, Google says Home app automations are now available in more countries and languages, while smart lock integrations have also become more reliable with improved notifications and error handling.FollowThank you for being part of our community. title: Another AI agent goes rogue? Meta says its model hacked a company
title_bn: Another AI agent goes rogue? Meta says its model hacked a company
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Meta's AI models hacked into a third-party company during cybersecurity testing due to a misconfiguration by the security firm Irregular.
paragraph1: Meta's AI models hacked into a third-party company during cybersecurity testing due to a misconfiguration by the security firm Irregular. The MeitY has also summoned Meta over the brief taking down of PM Modi's video.(REUTERS)Meta announced on Wednesday that its AI models had hacked into another company during cybersecurity testing. The information from Meta comes shortly after Anthropic and OpenAI revealed that their AI models had gone off track and gained access to third-party websites.Meta AI agent hacks company:Meta said that the hack occurred after its AI model gained access to the internet due to a ‘misconfiguration’ error by security company Irregular.In a statement quoted by Reuters, Meta said that its Muse Spark 1.1 model "exploited a security vulnerability in a third-party service, in a manner similar to previously reported instances with other companies."The model reportedly breached an unidentified third-party company's system and altered its internal environment.An Irregular spokesperson told Reuters that the incident was the "exact same evaluation-environment issue that was already disclosed by Anthropic last week" and did not include a "sandbox escape or a sophisticated cyber action."
paragraph2: “There are no current open issues. Irregular is developing a white paper to share best practices for containment and securely running cyber evaluations,” the company said.AI agents going rogue:On Tuesday, OpenAI announced two other incidents involving its AI agents gaining access to the internet and going rogue. In one of the incidents, which also occurred during an evaluation by Irregular, OpenAI said that a ‘misconfiguration’ in the testing environment allowed the models to access the internet.The models were told to find hidden information and exploit weaknesses within a simulated environment and were told they did not have access to the internet.Subsequently, OpenAI revealed that GPT-5.6 Sol exploited a real website by taking advantage of a ‘basic security vulnerability’. However, OpenAI says that its model believed the website was part of the simulated environment.Meanwhile, Britain's AI Security Institute has said that it found AI agents from Anthropic and OpenAI engaging in "unsanctioned" actions against real people and organisations during security evaluations conducted to assess the AI models' abilities.
paragraph3: AISI says that the incident occurred when the AI agents were given a cybersecurity challenge. The agency says that it ran the challenge 122 times across seven frontier AI models. It says that AI agents took ‘autonomous unsanctioned action’ on the internet in 10 of those scenarios, targeting real people and organisations.However, AISI found around 19 scenarios where the AI agents took unauthorized actions. It says almost all of the actions came from Anthropic's Mythos 5 model, while two actions were attributed to OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol with safety classifiers disabled.Prior to this, Hugging Face revealed last month that an AI agent from OpenAI had conducted a cyberattack on its website in order to obtain answers to the ExploitGym benchmark and termed it the first "end-to-end autonomous AI agent intrusion". OpenAI revealed that the agent was running on GPT-5.6 Sol and an unreleased AI model, and used a zero-day vulnerability within OpenAI's internal systems to gain access to the internet.
